websiteNote: From 14 pages of their campaign website, including its issues section.

Jobs and the economy.summary: Says they would help small businesses and local entrepreneurs with financing, training, and access to markets.
Jobs and the economy.quote: Supporting the creation, expansion, and sustainability of small businesses & local entrepreneurs through financing, training, and market access.

Schools and education.summary: Says they would invest in early childhood education, apprenticeships, and training in technology and the trades.
Schools and education.quote: Our government should invest in our people. Early childhood education, hands-on apprenticeships, and training in both technology and the trades will prepare our children and our workforce for tomorrow.

Health care.summary: Says they would expand access to affordable health care and lower out-of-pocket costs.
Health care.quote: Expand access to quality, affordable healthcare and lowering out-of-pocket costs for individuals and working families.

Energy and the environment.summary: Says they would add more affordable housing and bring down home energy costs.
Energy and the environment.quote: Increase the availability of safe, affordable housing options for homeowners, renters, and first-time buyers while also bringing energy costs within the home down.

Roads and infrastructure.summary: Says they would expand reliable high-speed internet, especially in rural and underserved areas.
Roads and infrastructure.quote: Increase access to reliable high-speed internet, particularly in underserved and rural areas, to support workforce operations and education.

Elections and government.summary: Says they would reform campaign finance and require accurate public reporting of political spending.
Elections and government.quote: Establish finance reform in the process of campaigns, disclosing political spending accurately to voters.

Taxes and spending.summary: Says tariffs work as taxes that Arkansans pay to the federal government.
Taxes and spending.quote: Say what you will, color it how you want to — tariffs at the end of the day are taxes. And Arkansans don’t like paying taxes to the federal government.
